doc.title: Karolina Strassmayer interviewed by Monk Rowe, May 25, 2023

chapter: New York and the WDR Big Band
title: Programs and writers: Mike Abene, Mendoza and others
summary: The band's weekly varied programs and Michael Abene's writing for doubles have educated her ears.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: What a thrill to sit down and get a new piece passed out to you by Mike Abene or any of these fantastic writers.

It is absolutely a thrill and it has really been also such an education for me as a musician to be immersed in all these different sounds and every week something different. A couple of weeks ago we just did a program with Vince Mendoza — he arranged Michel LeGrand’s music. Next week Bob Minter is coming and we’re playing a program of funk music and it’s — and especially Michael Abene, you mentioned Michael, he is such a hero to me. He’s maybe ten years or eleven years that he was our principal conductor. I think he wrote over one thousand arrangements for the band. And to just be right in the middle of that and play these beautiful sounds that he concocts and he has such a hand for writing for doubles and for all the different sounds. You know he uses euphoniums and flugels and tuba and of course in the woodwinds I mean sometimes we have to switch instruments like fifteen times in one arrangement you know it’s like just going back and forth. But he’s not just doing this to torture us, he really gets beautiful nuances and colors
out of a big band. And my ears have really, really opened up because I have had the opportunity to play all this different stuff. It’s a real privilege.
